Date: 13/09/2026

## GOHREP

**Goal:**

Test whether combining several trained scorers beats using one. Seven ensembles are
tried. Each starts from something observed about the models, not from ensembling being
a standard technique.

**Hypothesis:**

Combining will not raise accuracy much. Every member is trained on the same 1,834 crops,
and `analyses/10` §3 already found the top-100 CNNs give the same score as each other on
77.5% of test crops. Averaging cannot fix a mistake the members share.

One gain is expected, in §5. Cross-validated near-miss accuracy is 0.966 to 0.985 across
the tied members of all three grids, as recorded in each grid's
`random_search_results.csv`. So nearly all the remaining error is off by one. A rule that
can return the value *between* two neighbouring answers has something to use that a vote
does not.

§6 and §7 are both fitted to the 455 ensemble crops. So both should look good there and
lose most of it on test.

**Rationale:**

The seven ideas, one section each. "Known" means it was established before this analysis
and is cited. "Conjecture" means the section measures it before testing it.

| § | Idea | Why try it | Basis |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 2 | Vote over the 17 tied CNNs | At least one of 100 CNNs is right on 93% of test crops against 66% for the best one | Known (`analyses/10` §3.5) |
| 3 | Mix model families | A CNN, a transformer and a 12-feature regression may fail on different crops | Conjecture, measured in §3.1 |
| 4 | Mix training data, keep the architecture | The augmented CNNs were trained on a different set of crops | Known (`models/07` builds from `medoid_64_aug`) |
| 5 | Average the score instead of voting on it | Scores are ordered, and near-miss is 0.966-0.985, so nearly every error is off by one | Known (grid `avg_val_nearmiss`) |
| 6 | Pick members that disagree | Top-100 CNNs give the same score on 77.9% of crops, so members are near-duplicates | Known (`analyses/10` §3.5) |
| 7 | Learn who to trust at each score | Families may be good at different scores | Conjecture, measured in §7.1 |
| 8 | Decline the crops it is unsure about | Disagreement may mark the crops it gets wrong | Conjecture, measured in §8.1 |

Every choice, of members, rule, hyperparameters and committee size, is made on the
`ensemble` split (455 crops, never used in training). `test` (308 crops) is scored once at
the end. Both are shown, so the drop between them can be seen.

### 1.3 Check: do the cached predictions match what the grid searches recorded?

```{python}
# 1.3
# Each grid recorded a test_acc per config when it trained it. If this matrix is built
# right, the accuracy recomputed here must equal that number, model for model. Zero
# difference is the pass.
GRID = {
    "cnn": ROOT / "models/03_Medoid_CNN_RandomSearch/01_Categorical_Loss",
    "vit": ROOT / "models/04_Medoid_ViT_RandomSearch/01_Categorical_Loss",
    "geo": ROOT / "models/07_Medoid_CNN_GeomAug/01_MatchLargestClass",
}

def grid_table(tag):
    base = GRID[tag]
    frames = [pd.read_csv(base / "random_search_results.csv")]
    frames += [pd.read_csv(p) for p in (base / "parts").glob("*.csv")] if (base / "parts").exists() else []
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True).drop_duplicates("model_id").set_index("model_id")

RES = {tag: grid_table(tag) for tag in GRID}
MISMATCH = {}
for tag in GRID:
    ids = Z[f"{tag}_ids"]
    here = (Z[f"{tag}_t"].argmax(2) == yt[None, :]).mean(1)
    rec = RES[tag].reindex(ids)["test_acc"].to_numpy(float)
    ok = ~np.isnan(rec)
    off = np.abs(here - rec) > 1e-6
    MISMATCH[tag] = off
    print(f"{tag}: matched {ok.sum()}/{len(ids)}  models differing {int(off.sum())}  "
          f"max |here - recorded| = {np.abs(here[ok] - rec[ok]).max():.5f} "
          f"= {np.abs(here[ok] - rec[ok]).max() * len(yt):.1f} crops of {len(yt)}")
```

```{python}
# 1.3b
# Six ViTs come out one crop of 308 different. Check whether they are the models whose
# top two scores were closest together, which would make a single flip a rounding
# difference rather than a wrong matrix.
gap = lambda Q: np.diff(np.sort(Q, 2)[..., -2:], axis=2)[..., 0]   # top-1 minus top-2
gv, off = gap(Z["vit_t"]), MISMATCH["vit"]
print(f"smallest top-2 softmax margin, median over models")
print(f"  the {int(off.sum())} ViTs that differ: {np.median(gv[off].min(1)):.2e}")
print(f"  the {int((~off).sum())} that agree:    {np.median(gv[~off].min(1)):.2e}")
```

```{python}
# 1.4
```

### 1.5 Who is in the pool

```{python}
# 1.5
# A grid's single best config is not reproducibly the best: on 2,289 cross-validation
# crops the standard error near 0.65 is about 1.0 pp, and each grid has many configs
# inside that of its own winner. So each family contributes every config within one
# standard error of its own best. That rule reads cross-validation only and never touches
# `ensemble` or `test`.
#
# Every grid is ranked on avg_vaf, including models/07. The augmented pool is topped up to
# 1,627 crops per class, so avg_vaf there is measured on the same class balance as the
# 308-crop test split, while avg_vaf_orig is measured on the originals alone and those are
# 42.6% score 0 against the test split's 14.3%. Over the whole geometric grid avg_vaf
# correlates 0.838 with test accuracy against avg_vaf_orig's 0.808, and stays ahead in the
# top 2,000, 1,000 and 500. The cGAN grid is the exception and keeps avg_vaf_orig: only
# 10.9% of its pool is real, so its avg_vaf is largely accuracy on generated crops, which
# section 10 of analyses/06 shows does not transfer.
SE_CV = lambda p, n=2289: float(np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n))
RANK_ON = {"cnn": "avg_vaf", "vit": "avg_vaf", "geo": "avg_vaf"}
NICE = {"cnn": "CNN", "vit": "ViT", "geo": "CNN (geom. aug)"}

# Every CNN-family grid trains reg=None once per reg_strength, so 1,920 of its 8,640 runs
# repeat a setting the grid already holds. Collapsing to distinct settings first stops one
# setting taking several of the tie's places and voting several times. The ViT grid is
# built as two sub-grids and is unchanged by this.
FAM = {}
tie_report = []
for tag in GRID:
    col = RANK_ON[tag]
    settings = deduplicate(RES[tag].reset_index(), col).set_index("model_id")
    full = settings[col].dropna()
    cut = full.max() - SE_CV(full.max())
    tied_ids = set(full[full >= cut].index)
    have = Z[f"{tag}_ids"]
    assert len(set(have.tolist())) == len(have), f"duplicate model_id in the {tag} cache"
    keep = np.array([i for i, m in enumerate(have) if m in tied_ids])
    FAM[NICE[tag]] = {"e": Z[f"{tag}_e"][keep], "t": Z[f"{tag}_t"][keep], "ids": have[keep]}
    tie_report.append({"family": NICE[tag], "runs in grid": len(RES[tag]),
                       "distinct settings": len(full),
                       "best CV": round(float(full.max()), 4), "1 SE": round(SE_CV(full.max()), 4),
                       "tied": len(tied_ids), "tied & saved": len(keep)})

# The ordinal regression from analyses/03: one fit, so no tie set. Its class probabilities
# were exported by that analysis on both splits from the same train+val fit.
nd = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "analyses/03_feature_classifiers/model_cache/nondl_heldout_predictions.csv")
PCOL = [f"p{k}" for k in range(7)]
nde = nd[nd.split == "ensemble"].set_index("image_id").reindex(files_e)
ndt = nd[nd.split == "test"].set_index("image_id").reindex(files_t)
assert not nde[PCOL].isna().any().any() and not ndt[PCOL].isna().any().any()
assert (nde["true"].to_numpy() == ye).all() and (ndt["true"].to_numpy() == yt).all()
FAM["Ordinal regression"] = {"e": nde[PCOL].to_numpy(float)[None], "t": ndt[PCOL].to_numpy(float)[None],
                             "ids": np.array([0])}
tie_report.append({"family": "Ordinal regression", "runs in grid": 1,
                   "distinct settings": 1, "best CV": np.nan,
                   "1 SE": np.nan, "tied": 1, "tied & saved": 1})
pd.DataFrame(tie_report)
```

### 1.6 Metrics

```{python}
# 1.6
def exact(pred, y):
    return float(np.mean(pred == y))

def near(pred, y):
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(pred - y) <= 1))

def mae(pred, y):
    """Mean absolute error in score units. The natural loss for an ordinal target: it
    charges a 0-scored-as-6 seven times what it charges a 3-scored-as-4, which neither
    exact nor near-miss accuracy does."""
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(pred - y)))

def plurality(P):
    """P: (models, images) hard scores -> the modal score per image."""
    return np.array([np.bincount(P[:, j], minlength=7).argmax() for j in range(P.shape[1])])

def mean_prob(Q):
    """Q: (models, images, 7) softmax -> argmax of the member-averaged distribution."""
    return Q.mean(0).argmax(1)

def expected_score(Q):
    """Q -> the mean of the averaged distribution, rounded to the nearest score."""
    return np.clip(np.rint((Q.mean(0) * np.arange(7)).sum(1)), 0, 6).astype(int)

def family_mean(Qs):
    """Average within each family first, then across families, so a 51-model family
    does not outvote a 1-model family purely by count."""
    return np.stack([q.mean(0) for q in Qs]).mean(0)[None]

SE_E, SE_T = np.sqrt(0.65 * 0.35 / len(ye)), np.sqrt(0.65 * 0.35 / len(yt))
print(f"1 SE on the ensemble split ({len(ye)} crops) = {100 * SE_E:.2f} pp")
print(f"1 SE on the test split ({len(yt)} crops)     = {100 * SE_T:.2f} pp")
```

```{python}
# 1.6b
RNG = np.random.default_rng(0)
BOOT = RNG.integers(0, len(yt), size=(10000, len(yt)))

def paired_ci(a, b, y=None):
    """95% CI and two-sided p for accuracy(a) - accuracy(b) over the same crops."""
    y = yt if y is None else y
    da, db = (a == y).astype(float), (b == y).astype(float)
    d = da[BOOT].mean(1) - db[BOOT].mean(1)
    p = min(1.0, 2 * min((d <= 0).mean(), (d >= 0).mean()))
    return float(da.mean() - db.mean()), float(np.quantile(d, .025)), float(np.quantile(d, .975)), float(p)
```

## 2. Vote over the 17 tied CNNs

```{python}
# 2.1
# Take the CNNs cross-validation cannot separate. How often is at least one of them right
# (the oracle), against how often the best one is?
Ce, Ct = FAM["CNN"]["e"].argmax(2), FAM["CNN"]["t"].argmax(2)
nC = Ce.shape[0]
frac_e = (Ce == ye[None, :]).mean(0)          # fraction of the tied CNNs correct, per crop
oracle_e = float((frac_e > 0).mean())
best_e = float((Ce == ye[None, :]).mean(1).max())
print(f"{nC} tied CNNs, ensemble split:")
print(f"  at least one correct : {oracle_e:.4f}")
print(f"  best single model    : {best_e:.4f}")
print(f"  gap                  : {oracle_e - best_e:.4f}")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "How often the 17 tied CNNs get a crop right. Dark bars are crops the vote gets right. The vote can only win where the correct score is the most common one."
# 2.2
# Before building anything: split the crops by how many members get them right. A vote
# returns the most common answer, so it can only win where the true score is that answer.
# If the oracle's extra crops sit where 3 or 4 members are right, no vote reaches
# them.
mode_right_e = plurality(Ce) == ye
bins = np.arange(0, nC + 2) - 0.5
counts_all, _ = np.histogram(frac_e * nC, bins=bins)
counts_win, _ = np.histogram(frac_e[mode_right_e] * nC, bins=bins)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 3.6))
x = np.arange(nC + 1)
ax.bar(x, counts_all, color="#c9d6e8", label="Vote gets it wrong")
ax.bar(x, counts_win, color="#4C72B0", label="Vote gets it right")
ax.set_xlabel(f"Number of the {nC} tied CNNs that score the crop correctly")
ax.set_ylabel("Crops")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(THESIS_PLOTS / "oracle_decomposition.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

reach = frac_e[(frac_e > 0) & ~mode_right_e]
print(f"crops the oracle reaches but the vote does not: {len(reach)}")
print(f"  median fraction of members correct on them: {np.median(reach):.3f} "
      f"({np.median(reach) * nC:.1f} of {nC})")
print(f"  of those, the share with a minority (<50%) correct: {(reach < 0.5).mean():.3f}")
```

```{python}
# 2.3
R1 = {}
R1["Plurality vote, tied CNNs"] = (plurality(Ce), plurality(Ct))
R1["Mean softmax, tied CNNs"] = (mean_prob(FAM["CNN"]["e"]), mean_prob(FAM["CNN"]["t"]))
for k, (pe, pt) in R1.items():
    print(f"{k:28s} ensemble {exact(pe, ye):.4f}   test {exact(pt, yt):.4f}")
print(f"{'best single (on ensemble)':28s} ensemble {best_e:.4f}   test "
      f"{(Ct == yt[None, :]).mean(1)[np.argmax((Ce == ye[None, :]).mean(1))]:.4f}")
```

## 3. Mix model families

```{python}
# 3.1
# Two ways to measure whether models fail alike. Raw agreement is how often they give the
# same score. The joint-error ratio is how often both are wrong on the same crop, divided
# by how often they would be if their mistakes were unrelated. 1.0 means unrelated;
# higher means shared blind spots.
HARD_E = {k: v["e"].argmax(2) for k, v in FAM.items()}
HARD_T = {k: v["t"].argmax(2) for k, v in FAM.items()}
names = list(FAM)

def pair_stats(A, B, y, same):
    ag, ratio = [], []
    for i in range(A.shape[0]):
        for j in range(B.shape[0]):
            if same and j <= i:
                continue
            ag.append(np.mean(A[i] == B[j]))
            ea, eb = A[i] != y, B[j] != y
            indep = ea.mean() * eb.mean()
            ratio.append(np.mean(ea & eb) / indep if indep > 0 else np.nan)
    return np.array(ag), np.array(ratio)

rows = []
for i, a in enumerate(names):
    for b in names[i:]:
        if a == b and HARD_E[a].shape[0] < 2:
            continue
        ag, rt = pair_stats(HARD_E[a], HARD_E[b], ye, same=(a == b))
        rows.append({"pair": f"{a} vs {b}" if a != b else f"{a} (within)",
                     "kind": "within" if a == b else "across",
                     "n pairs": len(ag), "mean agreement": ag.mean(),
                     "joint-error / independent": np.nanmean(rt)})
corr = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("joint-error / independent")
corr.round(3)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "How often two models are wrong on the same crop, divided by how often they would be if their mistakes were unrelated. 1.0 (dashed) means unrelated."
# 3.2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 0.42 * len(corr) + 1.4))
cols = ["#C44E52" if k == "within" else "#4C72B0" for k in corr["kind"]]
ax.barh(range(len(corr)), corr["joint-error / independent"], color=cols)
ax.axvline(1.0, ls="--", color="grey", lw=1.2)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(corr)), corr["pair"], fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Joint error rate ÷ rate expected if errors were independent")
ax.set_xlim(0.95, corr["joint-error / independent"].max() * 1.06)
handles = [plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, color=c) for c in ("#C44E52", "#4C72B0")]
ax.legend(handles, ["Within one family", "Across families"], frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="lower right")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(THESIS_PLOTS / "error_correlation.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# 3.3
# Averaging all 84 members directly lets the 51 ViTs win on numbers, which is an accident
# of how many configs happened to tie. family_mean() averages inside each family first,
# then across the four, so each family carries the same weight.
R2 = {}
Qs_e, Qs_t = [FAM[n]["e"] for n in names], [FAM[n]["t"] for n in names]
R2["Family-balanced mean softmax (4 families)"] = (
    mean_prob(family_mean(Qs_e)), mean_prob(family_mean(Qs_t)))
allE, allT = np.concatenate(Qs_e), np.concatenate(Qs_t)
R2["Flat mean softmax (all 84 members)"] = (mean_prob(allE), mean_prob(allT))
R2["Plurality vote (all 84 members)"] = (plurality(allE.argmax(2)), plurality(allT.argmax(2)))
for k, (pe, pt) in R2.items():
    print(f"{k:44s} ensemble {exact(pe, ye):.4f}   test {exact(pt, yt):.4f}")
```

## 4. Mix training data, same architecture

```{python}
# 4.1
# Same-architecture-different-data (CNN + augmented CNN) against
# different-architecture-same-data (CNN + ViT), and against a completely different kind
# of model (CNN + ordinal regression). Two families each, so nothing else varies.
R3 = {}
pairs = {
    "CNN + ViT": ["CNN", "ViT"],
    "CNN + CNN (geom. aug)": ["CNN", "CNN (geom. aug)"],
    "CNN + Ordinal regression": ["CNN", "Ordinal regression"],
}
for k, fams in pairs.items():
    R3[k] = (mean_prob(family_mean([FAM[f]["e"] for f in fams])),
             mean_prob(family_mean([FAM[f]["t"] for f in fams])))
for k, (pe, pt) in R3.items():
    print(f"{k:28s} ensemble {exact(pe, ye):.4f}   test {exact(pt, yt):.4f}")
```

## 5. Average the score instead of voting on it

```{python}
# 5.1
# Scores are ordered and errors are nearly all off by one. A vote over seven unordered
# categories cannot use that: if members split between 3 and 5 it returns 3 or 5, never 4.
# First check there is any spread for an ordinal rule to work on.
Hb = allE.argmax(2)
share = np.array([np.bincount(Hb[:, j], minlength=7).max() for j in range(len(ye))]) / Hb.shape[0]
print(f"members backing the modal score, median {np.median(share):.3f}; "
      f"crops with no outright majority: {(share < 0.5).sum()} of {len(ye)}")
print(f"crops where the members span >= 2 scores: {np.mean([Hb[:, j].max() - Hb[:, j].min() >= 2 for j in range(len(ye))]):.3f}")
```

```{python}
# 5.1b
# Where the vote and the expected score differ, which is right more often?
FBe0 = family_mean(Qs_e)[0]
v_e, x_e = plurality(Hb), np.clip(np.rint((FBe0 * np.arange(7)).sum(1)), 0, 6).astype(int)
dis = v_e != x_e
print(f"the two rules disagree on {dis.sum()} of {len(ye)} ensemble crops ({dis.mean():.3f})")
print(f"  on those crops   vote exact {exact(v_e[dis], ye[dis]):.4f}  MAE {mae(v_e[dis], ye[dis]):.3f}")
print(f"                 expected exact {exact(x_e[dis], ye[dis]):.4f}  MAE {mae(x_e[dis], ye[dis]):.3f}")
print(f"  whole split      vote exact {exact(v_e, ye):.4f}  MAE {mae(v_e, ye):.3f}")
print(f"                 expected exact {exact(x_e, ye):.4f}  MAE {mae(x_e, ye):.3f}")
```

```{python}
# 5.2
# Three rules on identical members: the categorical vote, the argmax of the averaged
# distribution, and the expected score sum(k * p_bar(k)) rounded, which is ordinal
# throughout. np.rint rounds halves to even.
R4 = {}
FB_e, FB_t = family_mean(Qs_e), family_mean(Qs_t)
R4["Plurality vote (all 84 members)"] = (plurality(allE.argmax(2)), plurality(allT.argmax(2)))
R4["Family-balanced mean softmax (4 families)"] = (mean_prob(FB_e), mean_prob(FB_t))
R4["Family-balanced mean softmax, expected score rounded"] = (expected_score(FB_e), expected_score(FB_t))
for k, (pe, pt) in R4.items():
    print(f"{k:38s} ensemble exact {exact(pe, ye):.4f} near {near(pe, ye):.4f}   "
          f"test exact {exact(pt, yt):.4f} near {near(pt, yt):.4f}")
```

## 6. Pick members that disagree

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy against committee size. Members added greedily to maximise ensemble-split accuracy (blue), by ensemble-split rank (orange), or at random (grey, mean of 50). Solid = ensemble split, the one used to choose. Dashed = test."
# 6.1
# Add the member that most improves ENSEMBLE-SPLIT accuracy, one at a time. Test is never
# consulted, so the procedure is legitimate, but it is fitted to 455 crops. The question
# is how much of its gain survives. Two references: the same pool added by ensemble-split
# rank, and in random order.
POOL_E, POOL_T = allE, allT
K_MAX = 25

def acc_of(sel, Q, y):
    return exact(mean_prob(Q[sel]), y)

greedy, chosen = [], []
remaining = list(range(POOL_E.shape[0]))
for _ in range(K_MAX):
    scores = [acc_of(chosen + [m], POOL_E, ye) for m in remaining]
    best = remaining[int(np.argmax(scores))]
    chosen.append(best); remaining.remove(best)
    greedy.append((acc_of(chosen, POOL_E, ye), acc_of(chosen, POOL_T, yt)))
greedy = np.array(greedy)

rank_order = np.argsort(-(POOL_E.argmax(2) == ye[None, :]).mean(1))
ranked = np.array([(acc_of(list(rank_order[:k]), POOL_E, ye), acc_of(list(rank_order[:k]), POOL_T, yt))
                   for k in range(1, K_MAX + 1)])
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
rand = np.stack([[acc_of(list(o[:k]), POOL_T, yt) for k in range(1, K_MAX + 1)]
                 for o in (rng.permutation(POOL_E.shape[0])[:K_MAX] for _ in range(50))])

ks = np.arange(1, K_MAX + 1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 4.2))
ax.plot(ks, 100 * greedy[:, 0], color="#4C72B0", lw=1.8, label="Greedy on ensemble split")
ax.plot(ks, 100 * greedy[:, 1], color="#4C72B0", lw=1.5, ls="--", label="Greedy, on test")
ax.plot(ks, 100 * ranked[:, 0], color="#DD8452", lw=1.8, label="Ranked by ensemble accuracy")
ax.plot(ks, 100 * ranked[:, 1], color="#DD8452", lw=1.5, ls="--", label="Ranked, on test")
ax.plot(ks, 100 * rand.mean(0), color="grey", lw=1.3, ls="--", label="Random order, on test (mean of 50)")
ax.set_xlabel("Members in the committee"); ax.set_ylabel("Exact accuracy (%)")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, ncol=3, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.16))
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False); ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(THESIS_PLOTS / "greedy_selection.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

k_star = int(np.argmax(greedy[:, 0])) + 1
print(f"size chosen on the ensemble split: k = {k_star}")
print(f"  ensemble {greedy[k_star - 1, 0]:.4f}  ->  test {greedy[k_star - 1, 1]:.4f}  "
      f"(drop {100 * (greedy[k_star - 1, 0] - greedy[k_star - 1, 1]):.2f} pp)")
fam_of = np.concatenate([[n] * FAM[n]["e"].shape[0] for n in names])
print("  families in the chosen committee:", pd.Series(fam_of[chosen[:k_star]]).value_counts().to_dict())
print(f"  greedy at k=1 (i.e. the single best member) is already {greedy[0, 0]:.4f} on the "
      f"ensemble split; the whole curve spans {greedy[:, 0].min():.4f}-{greedy[:, 0].max():.4f}, "
      f"a range of {100 * (greedy[:, 0].max() - greedy[:, 0].min()):.2f} pp against a "
      f"{100 * SE_E:.2f} pp standard error")
print(f"  ranked order, starting from the same member: k=1 {ranked[0, 0]:.4f} -> "
      f"k=5 {ranked[4, 0]:.4f} -> k=25 {ranked[-1, 0]:.4f} on the ensemble split")
R5 = {f"Greedy selection (k={k_star}, chosen on ensemble)":
      (mean_prob(POOL_E[chosen[:k_star]]), mean_prob(POOL_T[chosen[:k_star]]))}
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Exact accuracy per severity score, by family, on the ensemble split."
# 7.1
ps = pd.DataFrame({n: [np.mean(HARD_E[n][:, ye == s] == s) for s in range(7)] for n in names},
                  index=range(7))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.0, 3.6))
w = 0.2
for i, n in enumerate(names):
    ax.bar(np.arange(7) + (i - 1.5) * w, ps[n], w, label=n, color=FAM_COL[n])
ax.set_xticks(range(7)); ax.set_xlabel("True severity score"); ax.set_ylabel("Exact accuracy")
```

```{python}
# 7.2
# Inputs are the four family-mean probability vectors, 28 numbers per crop. Kept small on
# purpose: the earlier version of this analysis stacked 100 one-hot model predictions,
# 700 inputs on 455 rows, which cannot be fitted honestly. Regularisation is chosen by
# 5-fold CV inside the ensemble split, and the ensemble figure reported is the
# cross-validated one, not resubstitution.
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold, cross_val_predict
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

Xe_st = np.concatenate([FAM[n]["e"].mean(0) for n in names], axis=1)
Xt_st = np.concatenate([FAM[n]["t"].mean(0) for n in names], axis=1)
CV = StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)

sweep = []
for C in [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0]:
    mk = lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=C, max_iter=5000))
    cvp = cross_val_predict(mk(), Xe_st, ye, cv=CV)
    tr = mk().fit(Xe_st, ye).predict(Xe_st)
    sweep.append({"C": C, "train (resub)": exact(tr, ye), "ensemble (5-fold CV)": exact(cvp, ye),
                  "gap": exact(tr, ye) - exact(cvp, ye)})
sw = pd.DataFrame(sweep)
C_star = float(sw.loc[sw["ensemble (5-fold CV)"].idxmax(), "C"])
print(f"chosen C = {C_star}")
sw.round(3)
```

```{python}
# 7.3  Leakage check: on permuted labels the combiner must collapse to chance (1/7).
mk = lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=C_star, max_iter=5000))
y_shuf = np.random.default_rng(7).permutation(ye)
shuf = exact(cross_val_predict(mk(), Xe_st, y_shuf, cv=CV), y_shuf)
print(f"shuffled-label CV accuracy {shuf:.3f} (chance {1 / 7:.3f}) -> "
      f"{'no leakage' if shuf < 0.20 else 'WARNING'}")

stack = mk().fit(Xe_st, ye)
R6 = {f"Logistic stack on family means (C={C_star})":
      (cross_val_predict(mk(), Xe_st, ye, cv=CV), stack.predict(Xt_st))}
for k, (pe, pt) in R6.items():
    print(f"{k:44s} ensemble {exact(pe, ye):.4f}   test {exact(pt, yt):.4f}")
```

## 8. Decline the crops the committee is unsure about

```{python}
# 8.1
# A committee has something no single model has: its own disagreement. If the crops the
# members argue about are the crops it gets wrong, the scorer can decline those and hand
# them to a human. First: does accuracy actually rise with agreement?
FBt = family_mean(Qs_t)[0]
conf_t = FBt.max(1)                                     # probability mass on the winning score
pred_t = FBt.argmax(1)
agree_t = np.array([np.mean(allT.argmax(2)[:, j] == pred_t[j]) for j in range(len(yt))])

rows = []
for lo, hi in [(0, .5), (.5, .7), (.7, .9), (.9, 1.01)]:
    m = (agree_t >= lo) & (agree_t < hi)
    if m.sum():
        rows.append({"member agreement": f"{lo:.0%}-{hi:.0%}", "crops": int(m.sum()),
                     "share": m.mean(), "exact": exact(pred_t[m], yt[m]),
                     "near-miss": near(pred_t[m], yt[m])})
pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy when the least-agreed crops are handed to a human instead of scored. Test split."
# 8.2
order = np.argsort(-agree_t)
cov = np.arange(1, len(yt) + 1) / len(yt)
acc_kept = np.cumsum(pred_t[order] == yt[order]) / np.arange(1, len(yt) + 1)
near_kept = np.cumsum(np.abs(pred_t[order] - yt[order]) <= 1) / np.arange(1, len(yt) + 1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.0, 4.0))
ax.plot(100 * cov, 100 * acc_kept, color="#4C72B0", lw=1.8, label="Exact")
ax.plot(100 * cov, 100 * near_kept, color="#55A868", lw=1.8, label="Near-miss (±1)")
ax.axhline(68.92, color="#C44E52", ls="--", lw=1.3, label="Human raters, exact (68.92%)")
ax.set_xlabel("Coverage: crops scored automatically (%)")
ax.set_ylabel("Accuracy on the crops kept (%)")
ax.set_xlim(10, 100); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="lower left")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False); ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(THESIS_PLOTS / "selective_prediction.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

# Many crops share an agreement value, so the order within a tie is arbitrary and the
# curve is jagged at that scale. The threshold table below avoids this by cutting on the
# agreement value itself rather than on a rank.
for c in (0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0):
    k = int(round(c * len(yt))) - 1
    print(f"  coverage {c:.0%}: exact {100 * acc_kept[k]:.2f}%  near-miss {100 * near_kept[k]:.2f}%")
print(f"  coverage at which the committee matches the human raters' 68.92%: "
      f"{100 * cov[np.max(np.where(acc_kept >= 0.6892))]:.0f}%"
      if (acc_kept >= 0.6892).any() else "  never reaches the human rate")
```

```{python}
# 8.3
# The threshold has to be picked without looking at test. Choose the agreement cut that
# hits a target accuracy on the ensemble split, apply it unchanged to test, and see
# whether coverage and accuracy hold up.
FBe = family_mean(Qs_e)[0]
pred_e = FBe.argmax(1)
agree_e = np.array([np.mean(allE.argmax(2)[:, j] == pred_e[j]) for j in range(len(ye))])
out = []
for target in (0.75, 0.80, 0.85):
    cand = sorted(set(agree_e))
    thr = next((t for t in cand if (agree_e >= t).sum() >= 20
                and exact(pred_e[agree_e >= t], ye[agree_e >= t]) >= target), None)
    if thr is None:
        out.append({"target exact (ensemble)": target, "threshold": np.nan}); continue
    me, mt = agree_e >= thr, agree_t >= thr
    out.append({"target exact (ensemble)": target, "threshold": round(thr, 3),
                "ens coverage": me.mean(), "ens exact": exact(pred_e[me], ye[me]),
                "test coverage": mt.mean(), "test exact": exact(pred_t[mt], yt[mt]),
                "test near-miss": near(pred_t[mt], yt[mt])})
pd.DataFrame(out).round(3)
```

## 10. Interpretation and Discussion

- **The oracle's lead is not accuracy waiting to be used (§2).** At least one of the 17
  tied CNNs is right on 89.23% of ensemble crops, against 63.96% for the best single one.
  None of that can be reached. On every crop where some member is right but the vote is
  not, the correct score is a *minority* answer, given by a median of 4 of the 17 members.
  A vote returns the most common answer, so it cannot reach those crops. The vote scores
  64.94% on test, against 64.61% for the best single member.
- **Different kinds of model do fail differently, but it is not worth much (§3).** The four
  lowest joint-error ratios are all between kinds of model, with CNN and ViT lowest at
  1.753. The two highest are within one kind (augmented CNN 2.194, CNN 1.923). Mixing all
  four gives 66.88% on test. That is 3.9 pp above the average single member, and level with
  the best one.
- **Different training data makes models less correlated than a different architecture
  does (§4).** CNN against augmented CNN is 1.919, and CNN against ViT is 1.753. The same
  architecture on different crops stays more alike than a different architecture on the
  same crops. The accuracies agree. CNN with augmented CNN is the worst pair, at 65.91%,
  below CNN with ViT at 67.53% and CNN with ordinal regression at 68.51%.
- **Averaging the score beats voting on it (§5).** The two rules differ on 54 of 455
  ensemble crops. On those, the average is right 53.70% of the time, against 42.59% for
  the vote, with mean error 0.463 against 0.611. It wins on the split used to choose
  (65.49%, against 65.49% for the argmax and 64.18% for the vote). It stays ahead on test,
  with 68.83% exact and mean error 0.325, both the best of any rule here. Its near-miss
  accuracy, 98.70%, is *not* the best. The chapter's single model reaches 99.03%.
- **Picking members that disagree does not work (§6).** Greedy selection's first pick is
  already the best single member, at 70.33%. Over 25 steps the curve only moves between
  69.67% and 70.77%. That range of 1.10 pp is small against a standard error of 2.24 pp, so
  choosing k is choosing noise. Its committee of k = 3 drops 5.83 pp on test, while the
  average rule *gains* 0.34 pp. Adding members to a lucky model, on the split that made it
  look lucky, does not help either. The ranked curve starts at the same 70.33% and falls to
  68.57% by five members.
- **A learned combiner cannot use the differences between scores (§7).** The differences
  are real. On score 2, the ordinal regression reaches 0.569 against the CNNs' 0.452, and on
  score 5, 0.662 against 0.521. But 455 rows need strong regularisation (C = 0.01). By
  C = 10, the gap between training and CV is 8.6 pp. It gains 0.97 pp on test, with a CI of
  −2.92 to +4.87. Shuffled labels give 0.156, against a chance rate of 0.143. So the fit is
  real, just small.
- **Declining uncertain crops is the one thing a committee can do that a single model
  cannot (§8).** Accuracy rises from 47.4% on the 19 crops where under half the members
  agree, to 79.1% on the 129 where over 90% agree. Thresholds set on the ensemble split
  carry over. The cut that gives 75.4% at 61.5% coverage there gives 75.1% at 60.1% on
  test. Declining the 10% with least agreement lifts the committee from 66.88% to 69.31%,
  just above the human raters' 68.92%. Declining half gives 76.62%.
- **No rule beats a good single model, but every rule beats a badly chosen one (§9).**
  Every paired-bootstrap interval includes zero, and the smallest p is 0.34. The one
  significant comparison goes the other way. The model that looked best on the ensemble
  split, at 70.33% there, falls to 62.34% on test. That is 4.55 pp below the chapter's
  chosen model, with a CI of −8.77 to −0.33 and p = 0.040. Single models from this pool
  range from 56.82% to 67.53% on test, while every fixed rule lands between 64.94% and
  68.83%. Combining removes the risk of picking the wrong model. It does not raise the
  ceiling.

### Recommendation

Two things are worth taking into the chapter, for different reasons:

1. **The mean softmax, balanced across kinds of model and decided by expected score (§5).**
   It has the highest exact accuracy and lowest mean error of anything tested. It also won
   on the split used to choose it. The ordered labels justify it, not its score. Report it
   as level with the best single model, not above it.
2. **The declining curve (§8).** This is the only result where a committee does something a
   single model cannot.

Everything else here is a negative result with a reason, and fits in one paragraph.

### Caveats

- The test split has 308 crops, so one standard error is 2.72 pp. Rules within about 5 pp
  of each other cannot be told apart.
- 13 rules were scored on 455 selection crops, so the best of them is optimistic by design.
  §9.4 measures that rather than ignoring it.
- The augmented grid contributes all 16 of its tied settings. `TopNStore`
  (`src/results_store.py`) saves weights for the top 100 runs by `avg_vaf`. The tie uses
  the same measure, so a tied setting always has saved weights. Earlier runs of this
  analysis saw only 15, because only 17 of the grid's 100 saved models had been copied from
  the cluster.
- The cGAN-augmented grid is left out because of the Results P11 finding. The soft-label
  grid now has its 100 saved models on disk, and its 10-member tie is fully covered. So it
  could be added as a fifth kind of model. It is left out because no paragraph needs it
  yet.
- The labels are the recorded median human scores. `analyses/10` §4 shows they are wrong on
  a handful of test crops.
